summary: Exact R(2^k−1) for all k ≤ 61 via a dedicated divisor search (for u ≤ v put w = 4Cu−1 = (n+u)/v, sieve-factor n+u for u ≤ √n/2; ~25 CPU-min total; matches the 1e8 census for k ≤ 26 and an independent sympy check R(2^33−1) = 44): R = 0 exactly at k ∈ {2,3,4,5,7,8,13} and R > 0 for every 14 ≤ k ≤ 61 (CERTIFIED; e.g. R = 228 at k = 61, minimum over 30 ≤ k ≤ 61 is 22 at k = 31). Mechanism (PROVED, elementary): no (★) solution n = 4Cuv−u−v of a Mersenne n has u or v in B_k = {1,2} ∪ {2^i+1 : i ≡ k (mod 2)}, because then the needed divisor w ≡ −1 (mod 4u) of n+u is an odd divisor of 2^k, of 2^k+1 (prime factors ≡ 1 mod 4, or ≡ 1,3 mod 8 for k odd) or of 2^{k−i}+1 with k−i even (all odd divisors ≡ 1 mod 4). Residue-matched controls n = 2^k−1+840j (200 per k ≤ 44, 40 per k ≤ 50) get 23% of R from min(u,v) ∈ B_k, and Mersenne R averages 0.70 × the control mean (k = 14..50; median percentile 0.18), so the zeros are this structural ~25–30% depletion plus small-n fluctuation (control means ≈ 9–14 at k ≤ 13), not a persistent obstruction.
not_done: The residual depletion beyond B_k (0.70 observed vs ≈0.77 predicted) is not explained; controls count only min(u,v) ∈ B_k, so the B_k share is a slight undercount; k > 61 not run.
next: Only if wanted: split R(2^k−1) by u to find the remaining structurally depleted u-classes (e.g. u with u−1 = 2^i·s, small s).

summary: The first step (U, R, Uv at 8 803 369) was already done in Pass 1 (U = 140, R = 16, I3 = 68, Uv = 11: not an R-zero or U-failure). Here a residue-matched control was added: among 40 primes ≡ 8 803 369 (mod 840) within ±1.1·10⁵, U ranges 131–366 (median 248) and only one has U < 140, so the greedy-record prime is U-hard (2nd lowest of 41) but not extreme. An independent C scan of v(p) = 4x(p) − p over all 4 904 759 399 primes < 1.2·10¹¹ (exact divisor-pair criterion: m/(px) is a sum of two unit fractions iff two divisors of px sum to 0 mod m; Pollard-rho factoring) reproduces A400619/A400620 exactly through the 9th term: records (p, v) = …, (118801, 59), (8 803 369, 107), (119 945 383 009, 111); the only other prime with v ≥ 100 is 45 195 081 409 (v = 103), CERTIFIED. The (★) count at the 9th term is R(119 945 383 009) = 56 (exact divisor search, scripts/z52d_p2_ZF0_Z0759_Rmersenne.c), so it is not an R-zero either.
not_done: U(119 945 383 009) itself (the linear count program needs ≈15 CPU-h at 1.2·10¹¹; no faster exact U counter written); Uv/I3 at the 9th term. The 1.2·10¹¹ scan took ≈37 min wall on 4 cores on an overloaded machine (load ≈ 37/24), slightly over the 30-min cap.
